title: Data Race Detection through Vibe Translation
problem: Existing data race detection tools (ThreadSanitizer, Archer) for C/Fortran+OpenMP have false negatives. Translate-then-check approach using AI models offers alternative detection strategy.
motivation: Traditional dynamic and static analysis tools miss some data races in OpenMP programs. Language translation using LLMs (vibe coding) provides different detection semantics that may catch races missed by original-language tools.
method: The approach converts C/Fortran+OpenMP programs into Go code using an AI language model following natural-language instructions (vibe coding). The translated Go code is then checked with Go's built-in data race detector, which monitors the program as it runs to catch conflicts where multiple threads access the same memory simultaneously. The team compares how well this method catches data races against existing tools like ThreadSanitizer and Archer that analyze the original code.
key_novelty: The approach translates code to Go using an AI model and checks it with Go's built-in data race detector, providing a complementary detection method that catches races existing tools miss.
contributions: AI-agent translation methodology for data race detection across languages
Evaluation framework comparing translate-then-check vs native detection
Accuracy and false negative rate analysis
limitations: Accuracy depends on translation quality; Go race detector may miss races invisible to it; limited to programs translatable to Go; no analysis of false positive rates
